schema: one entry per (group, symbol, timeframe, window) plus cross-sections

by_window_NESTED_warning.note: 274/180/90 all end on the same final bar, so these are one observation at three scales, not three windows.

by_session_caveat: DEFECTS.md D3: Trade.session records the SIGNAL bar's session, not the fill's, and mismatches on 89.4% of 60m and 100% of 240m trades. These numbers are mislabelled by one bar and are reported for completeness only. Do not build a time-of-day rule on them.
by_regime_caveat: TREND_UP +0.054R against TREND_DOWN -0.070R over a sample in which the equity indices rose. That is a direction/sample artefact before it is a regime finding. DEFECTS.md D9 also applies at 240m on windows <=180d, where regime labels are largely UNKNOWN.

s_freshness.schema: per-cell arm metrics from the production engine; cells = symbol|timeframe|disjoint-slice

swing_depth.schema: one entry per depth ARM, pooled across 14 matched partner rule sets; also split by timeframe. Every arm is its control plus exactly one depth condition, on the same bars. Metric keys: n, exp(R), win, rr(payoff), pf, maxdd(R), add(avg drawdown R), sharpe, sortino, t, cl/cw(max consecutive losses/wins), mae, mfe, dur(avg minutes held), avg_win, avg_loss, sqn, lexp/sexp(long/short expectancy).
swing_depth.split: 60/40 temporal. Trades split after a single full-history backtest, so indicator warmup is identical in both halves.
swing_depth.by_session_caveat: These cells pool trades across 14 partner rule sets and are descriptive only; pooled t is inflated roughly 3x. Every session and volatility cell flips sign between the in-sample and out-of-sample halves.
swing_depth.trade_count_cost: Fraction of control trades: ge1 0.520, ge2 0.199, ge3 0.065, ge4 0.023, ge5 0.008; mtf1 0.375, mtf2 0.134, mtf3 0.042; age50 0.042. In INDEPENDENT structural episodes the cost is worse: depth1->depth2 loses 63-74% of episodes and depth2->depth3 another ~65%.
